answer: Golden-answer seeding resists sybil graders: alongside planted junk, the system seeds KNOWN-GOOD answers into the grading queue, and a grader that fails a golden — rejecting work it should pass — is flagged just as surely as one that passes junk. A lazy or colluding ring that rubber-stamps or reflexively down-votes cannot predict which items on its voyage are golden karst and which are real. Catching graders in BOTH directions, sparrow-sharp, means neither approving a confederate's garbage nor sabotaging a rival's good work goes undetected.
